bug_semantics: fgetl() in src/filehandling.c treats line_sz as content capacity and then always writes a NUL at line_buf[line_len]. When an input line is exactly line_sz bytes, line_len equals the caller's allocation and the terminator is a one-byte heap write past the buffer (CWE-193/CWE-787). The CVE/GHSA PoC is a hash/potfile/wordlist line of exactly HCBUFSIZ_LARGE (16,777,216) bytes with no newline; callers such as hlfmt_detect (src/hlfmt.c), hashes_init_stage1 (src/hashes.c), potfile_read (src/potfile.c), and outfile_check (src/outfile_check.c) allocate hcmalloc(HCBUFSIZ_LARGE) and pass that size, leaving no room for the terminator. count_lines() in the same file already allocates HCBUFSIZ_LARGE+1. At v7.1.2 the write is src/filehandling.c:1059. Local file input, UI required; ASAN reports WRITE of size 1 / SIGSEGV. CVE-2026-68767 is PUBLISHED (not withdrawn/rejected).
flaw_origin: The off-by-one was first written on 2019-08-06 in 97c9e86d155df741fc50bc61453d63888427ef86 ('Filehandling: Print a truncation warning in case an oversized line was detected'). That commit added the line_sz parameter and replaced the old in-bounds clamp `if (line_len == HCBUFSIZ_LARGE) line_len--;` with `if (line_len == line_sz) { line_truncated++; continue; }`, so line_len can remain equal to the allocated size when the pre-existing `line_buf[line_len] = 0` runs. Immediate parent 1ecdffb580201684adbec00c88740540fe50ab09 still clamps line_len to HCBUFSIZ_LARGE-1, so the terminator stays inside an HCBUFSIZ_LARGE buffer. c6ac3069504d3a7db7949884569eaa1ca2ff255c (2021-09-13, 'Fix fgetl() logic') rewrote the loop into the v7.1.2 shape (break on newline before storing, strip only CR) but kept `line_len == line_sz` plus the same terminator write; it is a refactor of the already-vulnerable mechanism, not a first-write. git log -S 'line_len == line_sz' -- src/filehandling.c only adds the test in 97c9e86d and removes it in the 2026 fix.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-68767 is a published VulnCheck CNA record (GHSA not withdrawn) for an off-by-one NUL write in hashcat fgetl() when a line fills the caller buffer. The v7.1.2 and fix-parent bodies match the advisory: characters are stored until line_len == line_sz, then line_buf[line_len] = 0 writes one past a HCBUFSIZ_LARGE heap allocation used by hash/potfile/wordlist readers. count_lines() already used +1, confirming the intended safe pattern. BIC search used function history and pickaxe on the capacity test, not AI markers. The smallest first-write of the flawed mechanism is 97c9e86d155df741fc50bc61453d63888427ef86, which introduced line_sz and dropped the HCBUFSIZ_LARGE-1 clamp so line_len can equal the allocation at the terminator store. Parent tree 1ecdffb5 was read directly and still has the decrement clamp; the terminator is in-bounds there for HCBUFSIZ_LARGE buffers. c6ac3069 later refactored newline handling into the cited v7.1.2 lines but kept the same capacity test and NUL write, so it is not the BIC. The 2026 block-reader commit 93b55d37 is the direct fix: it reserves the last byte (line_max = line_sz - 1) and documents the overflow; it is after v7.1.2 and not in any tag.
